svg.aria-label: Diagram: the two Private Google Access virtual IP address domains in Google Cloud and the DNS records behind them; private.googleapis.com occupies 199.36.153.8/30 with an IPv6 range, and restricted.googleapis.com occupies the adjacent 199.36.153.4/30 with its own IPv6 range, each a slash thirty holding four addresses which is exactly the number of A records the documentation lists for each; private covers most Google APIs including Maps, Ads and Cloud regardless of VPC Service Controls support but excludes Workspace web applications, while restricted covers only APIs that support VPC Service Controls and actively blocks those that do not, excluding Workspace APIs as well; the default domains are a third option needing no DNS configuration at all because they use ordinary public addresses and are the only option covering Workspace web applications; the records to create are four A records plus an AAAA record for the chosen domain and a wildcard CNAME pointing all of googleapis.com at it, with the same A-plus-wildcard-CNAME pattern repeated for other domains such as gcr.io; routing and firewall rules must cover the direct connectivity range as well as the VIP range itself; and the protocol restriction that these VIPs carry only HTTP-based protocols over TCP, so MQTT and ICMP are unsupported and the addresses cannot be pinged
svg.title: Restricted and private VIPs: two adjacent /30s, four A records each, and HTTP only
svg.text: Two adjacent /30s that decide which half of Google you can reach.
The choice is not about addressing. It is about VPC Service Controls, stated as a range.
private.googleapis.com
• MOST Google APIs, regardless of
VPC Service Controls support
• Includes Maps, Ads, Google Cloud
• NOT Workspace web apps
(Gmail, Google Docs)
Choose it if you don’t use VPC SC, or
need APIs VPC SC doesn’t support.
restricted.googleapis.com
• ONLY APIs supported by VPC
Service Controls
• BLOCKS those that do not support it
• NOT Workspace APIs either, nor the
web apps
Choose it when you need ONLY the
VPC SC-supported set. Blocking is the point.
And a third option that is neither: the DEFAULT DOMAINS
Ordinary public addresses, so NO special DNS configuration is required. Used whenever you
don’t configure records for the two VIP domains — and the ONLY option covering Workspace web apps.
The records behind them — four A records, because a /30 is four addresses
private.googleapis.com → A: 199.36.153.8, .9, .10, .11
restricted.googleapis.com → A: 199.36.153.4, .5, .6, .7
• Plus an AAAA record to the matching IPv6 address, for IPv6 clients
• Then a CNAME for *.googleapis.com pointing at whichever domain you chose
• Repeat the pattern per extra domain: A for DOMAIN, CNAME *.DOMAIN → DOMAIN
e.g. a CNAME for *.gcr.io pointing to gcr.io
HTTP only — and that includes the tool you were about to reach for
These VIPs support ONLY HTTP-BASED PROTOCOLS OVER TCP: HTTP, HTTPS and HTTP/2.
ALL OTHER PROTOCOLS, INCLUDING MQTT AND ICMP, ARE NOT SUPPORTED.
So a failed ping proves nothing — ping was never going to work. Interactive websites and
features that use the internet, such as redirects or retrieving content, are unsupported too.
Routing and firewall cover MORE than the VIP range
For either domain, the routes and egress rules must also reach the direct-connectivity range
from #90 — the APIs that bypass the Google Front Ends do not use the VIP.
Allow the VIP range AND that range, or part of your API surface silently fails.
Two exclusions to read before you point a wildcard at either domain
Neither VIP serves *.rep.googleapis.com — the regional and multi-regional endpoints #90
already ruled out. A wildcard will capture those names and break them.
accounts.google.com works only for the paths needed for OAuth authentication of SERVICE
ACCOUNTS. User account authentication is interactive, and is not supported.
The two ranges are ADJACENT: .4–.7 is restricted, .8–.11 is private. One digit decides your API surface.
